name: The deck's market figure is accurate for a category it does not serve
description: An anchoring case. The deck says it is in AI observability, a $3.1B market growing 38%, and the corpus confirms exactly that for AI observability broadly [S1] — so a naive check 'verifies' the number and moves on. The frame is the error: the corpus sizes the LLM application tracing slice this company actually sells into at $180-260M with growth decelerating to 20-25% [S2], and attributes the deceleration to model providers shipping tracing natively [S3]. A correct analysis refuses the deck's denominator even though a source supports the figure. Verifying the wrong proposition is the failure being tested.

claims.rationale: The figure is right for AI observability broadly [S1] and wrong for what this company sells. Accepting it as 'supported' is the anchoring failure: a source was cited, and it was a source for a different claim.

blind_spots.rationale: The slice the company actually serves, which the deck never sizes.
Model providers shipping tracing free is the reason growth decelerated.
Growth in the real slice is roughly a third of the rate the deck claims.
